newsitem.title: INDONESIA: Violence mars end to Indonesian election campaign.
newsitem.headline: Violence mars end to Indonesian election campaign.

text.p: Rioters torched a top hotel and attacked churches on Borneo island and four people died on Java on the final day of Indonesia's general election campaign on Friday, residents and news reports said on Saturday.
The official Antara news agency said at least four people died in violence at Bangil in eastern Java.

One resident contacted by phone said the four people were killed during a clash between supporters of the Moslem-oriented United Development Party (PPP) and security forces after the PPP attacked buildings in the town.
The resident said police fired warning shots, but it was not clear exactly how they had died. Police declined to comment.
Antara said 32 people had been treated for knife wounds, cuts and burns during rioting in Banjarmasin, capital of South Kalimantan province on the Indonesian side of Borneo.
Residents in Banjarmasin, a city of 400,000, said at least two people were killed but there was no immediate confirmation.
They said the violence started with fighting between supporters of the ruling Golkar and the PPP on the last day of campaigning for next Thursday's national and local elections.
The capital Jakarta and the satellite cities of Tangerang and Bekasi were also hit by street violence.

Antara reported other disturbances in Java, Indonesia's most populous island, at Solo and Semarang in the centre, Cirebon in the west as well as Bangil and Malang in the east. Ujung Pandang, capital of South Sulawesi province, also saw unrest.
There were no reports of trouble through the sprawling archipelago of 200 million people on Saturday, the first day of a five-day cooling off period before the polls.
Nearly 125 million people are eligible to cast their ballots on Thursday for 425 elected seats in the House of Representatives and for provincial and district assemblies.
The PPP, Golkar and the badly-split minority Indonesian Democratic Party (PDI) are the only three groups legally permitted to contest the elections, held every five years.
Golkar, in power for the last 30 years under President Suharto, took 68 percent of the vote at the last elections in 1992 and is expected to win next week's poll comfortably.
Church sources said at least seven churches were either burnt, looted or stoned in the South Kalimantan capital.

"Only one church was burnt, but all the churches in Banjarmasin suffered severe damage with all their possessions looted and the buildings stoned," one priest, who asked not to be named, told Reuters.

Kompas newspaper said a number of Golkar offices were either burnt or damaged and it reported extensive damage to shops after they were stoned. It said the four-star Hotel Kalimantan as well as a supermarket and a cinema were burnt.
"The damage is extraordinary," one resident told Reuters.
Residents said troops had been flown into Banjarmasin and that the situation was now calm and under control, although all shops and offices remained closed.
"Nothing is open. There are troops throughout the city," the resident said.
Police declined to comment on the riot but said the situation in Banjarmasin on Saturday was calm.
Kompas newspaper said the fighting started after Golkar loyalists began campaigning before Friday Islamic prayers, angering Moslems going to mosques, many of whom were PPP supporters.
